content:
anna: quick context — followup to the 'multi-region primaries' RFC. i want to prototype a small experiment where we rotate the primary region for low-risk tenants every 24h. goals: spread load, surface cross-region latencies, and see cost differences.

mike: curious about safety — what happens to KV cache and warmup? rotation could spike cold cache misses.

sachin: agree. we should preserve a small prefix cache TTL for tenants during rotation to avoid full cold starts. proposal: do a staged handoff: 1) shadow writes to new primary, 2) prewarm kv via async replication, 3) cutover.

katie: product concern: some customers require residency. we need an allowlist so rotation only applies to non-residency tenants. also include a config toggle per-tenant.

julia: legal: residency tenants must opt-out. also add audit events for every rotation (region-from, region-to, timestamp, operator).

anna: agreed. experiment scope: 300 tenants, low QPS, non-PII tag. rotation cadence = 24h first stage, then test 6h if stable.

mike: rollout plan suggestion: canary 24h -> monitor 6 metrics: 99th latency, cold-miss-rate, kv-sync-lag, error-rate, cost-per-token, tenant-slo-breaches. alert thresholds pre-configured.

sachin: infra changes needed: support a 'rotation handshake' endpoint on controlplane. pseudocode snippet:

```
POST /v1/control/rotate-primary
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "target_region": "us-west1",
  "phase": "prepare" // prepare | prewarm | promote | finalize
}
```

anna: nice. phases help operators abort mid-flow. need idempotency keys.

katie: UX: add tenant-level flag in console: "allow_primary_rotation" with opt-in description. default = false. show rotation history.

julia: add consent checkbox for EU tenants even if non-PII; better to be explicit.

mike: SRE ops: add a kill-switch to stop all rotations (global feature flag) + per-region drain policy to avoid double-promote if network blips.

sachin: KV concerns: use asynchronous replication to prefill destination edge cache, but we must handle write races. approach: shadow-writes with tombstone reconciliation window (30s) then promote.

anna: tradeoffs: faster rotation frequency -> better load distribution but higher cold misses and more complexity in rollback. slower rotations -> less churn but weaker load balancing.

katie: metric success criteria for experiment: no >1.5x increase in token-cost per request and <5% increase in tail latency for canary tenants. if either triggers, rollback.

mike: one more: instrumentation. add rotation_event tagging in traces and correlate tail-latency to rotation-phase. also capture prewarm-hit-rate metric.

sachin: infra checklist: controlplane endpoint, prewarm job, eviction guard on old primary for 2m after finalize, health-check gating. I'll sketch an ops runbook.

julia: legal asks for retention of rotation audit logs for 13 months for some regions. call this out in runbook.

anna: action items: 
- sachin: PR for handshake endpoint + prewarm job (due EOW)
- mike: alert playbook + kill-switch (EOW)
- katie: console flag + tenant opt-in UX copy (next Tues)
- julia: audit retention policy note (next Tues)
- anna: draft experiment brief and measurement dashboard (tomorrow)

rotations-bot: canary-run created: id=r-20240315-01, 300 tenants selected, start=2024-03-20T03:00Z

mike: quick question — how do we pick tenant rotation candidates? random stratified by region and qps?

anna: yes, stratified random by region + 95th-pct QPS < 50, non-residency tag, <30 days uptime.

sachin: edge-case: what about third-party integrations that assume static region header? add a preflight probe to detect header-based assumptions. if probe fails, exclude tenant.

katie: good call. put that probe in the canary gating.

anna: wrapping: keep experiment narrow, strong rollback, and surface early telemetry. i'll post the experiment brief to #product and link to this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: noted. will start building alerts. :gear:

sachin: will create PRs and link runbook.

julia: will draft the legal note.

anna: logging this here for traceability. we'll reconvene after first 48h of canary.
